editorial_note: Śrīdhara Svāmī only. Sanskrit is keyed to the pinned source; phrase-level glosses and literal English are source-bound. The explicit no-commentary marker at 3.32.15 is preserved; genuine source gaps remain marked separately.
scope: ŚB 3.32.1–3.32.43; all 37 Śrīdhara commentary blocks restored, with 3.32.15 explicitly recorded as not explained by the other three commentators.

entries.sanskrit:
द्वा-त्रिंशे सात्त्विकैर् धर्मैर् ऊर्ध्वं गतिर् उदीर्यते ।

तत्त्व-ज्ञान-विहीनस्य ततश् च पुनर् आगतिः ॥

तद् एवं पाप-कर्मणो गतिर् उक्ता, इदानीं काम्य-कर्मणो गतिम् आह---अथेति चतुर्भिः । यो गृह एवावसन् स्वान् धर्मान् दोग्धि । दोह्यम् आह---कामम् अर्थं च तान् दुग्धान् धर्मान् भूयः पिपर्ति पूरयत्य् अनुतिष्ठति ॥१॥
word_for_word: return of one lacking knowledge of reality
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration:
dvā-triṃśe sāttvikair dharmair ūrdhvaṃ gatir udīryate |

tattva-jñāna-vihīnasya tataś ca punar āgatiḥ ||

tad evaṃ pāpa-karmaṇo gatir uktā, idānīṃ kāmya-karmaṇo gatim āha---atheti caturbhiḥ | yo gṛha evāvasan svān dharmān dogdhi | dohyam āha---kāmam arthaṃ ca tān dugdhān dharmān bhūyaḥ piparti pūrayaty anutiṣṭhati ||1||
entries.literal_english: In the thirty-second chapter the upward course produced by sāttvika duties is described, followed by the return of one who lacks knowledge of reality. Having described the destination of sinful action, he now explains in four verses the destination of desire-motivated action. One who remains a householder “milks” his prescribed duties for desire and wealth, and then repeatedly nourishes and performs those duties for those ends.

entries.sanskrit: सोऽपि भगवद्-आराधन-रूपाद् धर्मात् पराङ्-मुखः सन् प्राकृतान् अपि देवान् पितॄंश् च यजते ॥२॥
word_for_word: turned away from dharma as worship of Bhagavān
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: so’pi bhagavad-ārādhana-rūpād dharmāt parāṅ-mukhaḥ san prākṛtān api devān pitṝṃś ca yajate ||2||
entries.literal_english: Such a person, turned away from dharma in the form of worship of Bhagavān, worships even the material gods and the ancestors.

entries.sanskrit: ततः किम् ? तत्राह---तेषां श्रद्धयाक्रान्ता व्याप्ता मतिर् यस्य । पित्र्-अर्थं देवार्थं च व्रतं नियमो यस्य । सोम-पाः, तत्र सोमं पीत्वेत्य् अर्थः ॥३॥
word_for_word: whose mind is pervaded by faith in them
पित्र्-अर्थं देवार्थं च व्रतं नियमो यस्य
whose vow is directed to the ancestors and the gods
entries.literal_english: What follows? He answers: the man’s mind is pervaded by faith in them; his vow is directed to the ancestors and the gods. “Soma-drinkers” means those who drink Soma.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: tataḥ kim ? tatrāha---teṣāṃ śraddhayākrāntā vyāptā matir yasya | pitr-arthaṃ devārthaṃ ca vrataṃ niyamo yasya | soma-pāḥ, tatra somaṃ pītvety arthaḥ ||3||

entries.sanskrit: लोके तिष्ठत्य् अपि पुण्य-क्षयात् पातम् उक्त्वा लोकानाम् अपि लयम् आह---यदा चाहरहः प्रलये ॥४॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: loke tiṣṭhaty api puṇya-kṣayāt pātam uktvā lokānām api layam āha---yadā cāharahaḥ pralaye ||4||
entries.literal_english: After saying that one falls from a world when merit is exhausted, he also describes the dissolution of those worlds at the daily pralaya.

entries.sanskrit: भगवद्-धर्म-निष्ठानां तत् प्राप्तिम् एव गतिम् आह त्रिभिः । ये तु कामार्थ-प्रयोजनाय स्व-धर्मान् न दुह्यन्ति न दुहन्ति । निःसङ्गा अनासक्ताः । न्यस्तान् ईश्वरे समर्पितानि कर्माणि यैः ॥५-६॥
word_for_word: of those established in Bhagavān’s dharma
do not milk duty for desire and wealth
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: bhagavad-dharma-niṣṭhānāṃ tat prāptim eva gatim āha tribhiḥ | ye tu kāmārtha-prayojanāya sva-dharmān na duhyanti na duhanti | niḥsaṅgā anāsaktāḥ | nyastān īśvare samarpitāni karmāṇi yaiḥ ||5-6||
entries.literal_english: In three verses he states that those established in Bhagavān’s dharma attain Him. They do not milk their own duties for the purposes of desire and wealth; they are unattached and have offered their actions to the Lord.

entries.sanskrit: विश्वतो-मुखं परिपूर्णं पुरुषं यान्ति । तथा च श्रुतिः---सूर्य-द्वारेण ते विरजाः प्रयान्ति यत्रामृतः पुरुषो ह्य् अव्ययात्मा इति । प्रकृतिम् उपादान-कारणम् । उत्पत्त्य् अन्त-भावनं निमित्त-कारणम् ॥७॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: viśvato-mukhaṃ paripūrṇaṃ puruṣaṃ yānti | tathā ca śrutiḥ---sūrya-dvāreṇa te virajāḥ prayānti yatrāmṛtaḥ puruṣo hy avyayātmā iti | prakṛtim upādāna-kāraṇam | utpatty anta-bhāvanaṃ nimitta-kāraṇam ||7||
entries.literal_english: They attain the all-faced, complete Puruṣa. Scripture likewise says that through the solar gate the stainless go where the immortal Puruṣa of imperishable Self abides. Prakṛti is the material cause, while that which brings about origination and dissolution is the efficient cause.

entries.sanskrit: परमेश्वर-दृष्ट्या हिरण्यगर्भोपासकानाम् अपि क्रमेण तत्-प्राप्तिम् आह---द्वि-परार्धावसान इति त्रिभिः । परस्य हिरण्यगर्भस्य । पर-चिन्तकाः परमेश्वर-दृष्ट्या हिरण्यगर्भोपासकाः ॥८॥
word_for_word: at the end of two parārdhas
those contemplating him as the Supreme
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: parameśvara-dṛṣṭyā hiraṇyagarbhopāsakānām api krameṇa tat-prāptim āha---dvi-parārdhāvasāna iti tribhiḥ | parasya hiraṇyagarbhasya | para-cintakāḥ parameśvara-dṛṣṭyā hiraṇyagarbhopāsakāḥ ||8||
entries.literal_english: He explains that even worshippers of Hiraṇyagarbha who view him as the Supreme Lord attain the Lord gradually, at the end of two parārdhas. “Of the supreme” here means of Hiraṇyagarbha; para-cintakāḥ are those who worship Hiraṇyagarbha with the vision of the Supreme Lord.

entries.sanskrit: क्ष्मादीनि पञ्च-महा-भूतानि मनश् चेन्द्रियाणि चार्थाश् च शब्दादयो भूतादिश् चाहङ्कारः एवम् आदिभिः परिवृतं युक्तं ब्रह्माण्डं प्रति संहर्तुम् इच्छुः सन् । अव्याकृतम् ईश्वरम् । पराख्यं द्वि-परार्ध-लक्षणं कालम् ॥९॥
word_for_word: earth and the other five great elements
desiring to withdraw the cosmic egg
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: kṣmādīni pañca-mahā-bhūtāni manaś cendriyāṇi cārthāś ca śabdādayo bhūtādiś cāhaṅkāraḥ evam ādibhiḥ parivṛtaṃ yuktaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ prati saṃhartum icchuḥ san | avyākṛtam īśvaram | parākhyaṃ dvi-parārdha-lakṣaṇaṃ kālam ||9||
entries.literal_english: Desiring to withdraw the cosmic egg surrounded by earth and the other five great elements, mind, senses, their objects such as sound, and ahaṅkāra, he enters the unmanifest Lord and the time called para, measured as two parārdhas.

entries.sanskrit:
परेत्य दूरं गत्वा भगवन्तं हिरण्यगर्भम् अनुप्रविष्टा ये योगिनोऽमृतं परमानन्द-रूपं प्रधानम् उत्कृष्टं ब्रह्म तेनैव सहोपयान्ति, न तु पूर्वम् । यस् तद्-आगताभिमानाः । तथा च स्मृतिः,

ब्रह्मणा सह ते सर्वे सम्प्राप्ते प्रतिसञ्चरे ।

परस्यान्ते कृतात्मानः प्रविशन्ति परं पदम् ॥ इति ॥१०॥
word_for_word: the yogis who have entered the Lord Hiraṇyagarbha
the yogis [approach] the immortal, principal Brahman whose form is supreme bliss
they approach together with him, not earlier
those who identify themselves with him
ब्रह्मणा सह ते सर्वे सम्प्राप्ते प्रतिसञ्चरे
at the cosmic dissolution, all those together with Brahman
having realized the Self, enter the supreme state at the end of the Supreme
entries.literal_english: Having gone far and entered the Lord Hiraṇyagarbha, the yogis approach the immortal, supreme Brahman, which is the highest form of bliss, together with him; they do not reach it earlier. They identify themselves with him. The Smṛti also says: “At the cosmic dissolution, all those who have attained Brahman together with him enter the supreme state at the end of the Supreme, having realized the Self.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration:
paretya dūraṃ gatvā bhagavantaṃ hiraṇyagarbham anupraviṣṭā ye yogino’mṛtaṃ paramānanda-rūpaṃ pradhānam utkṛṣṭaṃ brahma tenaiva sahopayānti, na tu pūrvam | yas tad-āgatābhimānāḥ | tathā ca smṛtiḥ,

brahmaṇā saha te sarve samprāpte pratisañcare |

parasyānte kṛtātmānaḥ praviśanti paraṃ padam || iti ||10||

entries.sanskrit: भगवद्-उपासकास् तु साक्षाद् एव तं प्राप्नुवन्ति न तु क्रमेण, अतस् त्वं साक्षात् तम् एव भजेत्य् आह---अथ तस्मात् । भावेन प्रेम्णा ॥११॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: bhagavad-upāsakās tu sākṣād eva taṃ prāpnuvanti na tu krameṇa, atas tvaṃ sākṣāt tam eva bhajety āha---atha tasmāt | bhāvena premṇā ||11||
entries.literal_english: Worshippers of Bhagavān attain Him directly, not gradually. Therefore, he tells Devahūti, worship Him directly. Bhāva means love.

entries.sanskrit: एवं तावद् भगवद्-भक्तानां निरन्तरम् एव तत्-प्राप्तिर् भगवद्-अभेदेन हिरण्यगर्भोपासकानां तु क्रमेणेत्य् उक्तम् । भेदेनोपासने तु ब्रह्मादयोऽप्य् आवर्तन्ते किम् उतान्य इत्य् आह---आद्य इति चतुर्भिः । यो वेद-गर्भः सोऽपि गुण-व्यतिकरे जाते यथा-पूर्वं ब्रह्म-पदाधिकृतः सन् प्रजायते इति तृतीयेनान्वयः । न केवलं स एवैकः, किन्तु ऋषिभिर् मरीच्य्-आदिभिर् योगेश्वरादिभिश् च सह ॥१२॥
word_for_word: when worship is based on difference
when disturbance of the guṇas occurs
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: evaṃ tāvad bhagavad-bhaktānāṃ nirantaram eva tat-prāptir bhagavad-abhedena hiraṇyagarbhopāsakānāṃ tu krameṇety uktam | bhedenopāsane tu brahmādayo’py āvartante kim utānya ity āha---ādya iti caturbhiḥ | yo veda-garbhaḥ so’pi guṇa-vyatikare jāte yathā-pūrvaṃ brahma-padādhikṛtaḥ san prajāyate iti tṛtīyenānvayaḥ | na kevalaṃ sa evaikaḥ, kintu ṛṣibhir marīcy-ādibhir yogeśvarādibhiś ca saha ||12||
entries.literal_english: Thus devotees of Bhagavān attain Him without interruption, while worshippers of Hiraṇyagarbha as nondifferent from Bhagavān attain Him gradually. But if worship is based on difference, even Brahmā and others return. When the guṇas become disturbed, the Veda-garbha Brahmā again takes birth, appointed to Brahmā’s station as before, together with sages such as Marīci and lords of yoga.

entries.sanskrit: जन्मनि हेतु-द्वयम् । भेद-दृष्ट्य्-आभिमानेन कर्तृत्वाद् इति च । यथा पूर्वत्वे हेतुः, निःसङ्गेन निष्कामेन कर्मणेति ॥१३॥
word_for_word: and agency arising from the perception and conviction of difference
just as the cause of the former state
is action performed without attachment and desire
entries.literal_english: There are two causes for birth: agency arising from the perception and conviction of difference, and—just as the cause of the former state was—action performed without attachment and desire.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: janmani hetu-dvayam | bheda-dṛṣṭy-ābhimānena kartṛtvād iti ca | yathā pūrvatve hetuḥ, niḥsaṅgena niṣkāmena karmaṇeti ||13||

entries.sanskrit: किं कृत्वात्र प्रजायते ? प्रथमं पारमेष्ठ्यम् ऐश्वर्यं निषेव्य, पश्चात् प्रलये स-गुणं गुणाधिष्ठातारं प्रथमावतार-रूपं पुरुषं संसृत्य प्राप्य, तेऽपि ऋषि-प्रमुखाः स्व-कर्म-निर्मितम् ऐश्वर्यं निषेव्य पुरुषं च संसृत्य यथा पूर्वं स्व-स्वाधिकारेण पुनर् आयान्तीत्य् अन्वयः ॥१४॥
word_for_word: what having done does one take birth here?
first, having enjoyed the sovereignty of Brahmā’s realm
स-गुणं गुणाधिष्ठातारं प्रथमावतार-रूपं पुरुषं संसृत्य प्राप्य
having reached the first avatāra, the Puruṣa who presides over the qualities together with the qualities
those sages, Brahmā and the others
having enjoyed sovereignty produced by their own actions
they return again, each to the former office
entries.literal_english: What having done do they take birth here? First they enjoy the sovereignty of Brahmā’s realm. Then at dissolution they reach the first avatāra, the Puruṣa who presides over the qualities together with the qualities. The sages headed by Brahmā likewise enjoy the sovereignty produced by their own actions, reach the Puruṣa, and then return again to their respective offices as before.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: kiṃ kṛtvātra prajāyate ? prathamaṃ pārameṣṭhyam aiśvaryaṃ niṣevya, paścāt pralaye sa-guṇaṃ guṇādhiṣṭhātāraṃ prathamāvatāra-rūpaṃ puruṣaṃ saṃsṛtya prāpya, te’pi ṛṣi-pramukhāḥ sva-karma-nirmitam aiśvaryaṃ niṣevya puruṣaṃ ca saṃsṛtya yathā pūrvaṃ sva-svādhikāreṇa punar āyāntīty anvayaḥ ||14||

entries.sanskrit: अन्यैस् त्रिभिर्न व्याख्यातम्।
word_for_word: Not explained by the other three commentators
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; under 3.32.15, following Madhva’s note, the source states अन्यैस् त्रिभिर्न व्याख्यातम् (“not explained by the other three commentators”).
entries.literal_english: No Śrīdhara commentary is supplied; the pinned source notes that the other three commentators did not explain this verse.

entries.sanskrit: यदा ब्रह्मोपासकानाम् अपि भेद-दर्शनाभिमानाभ्याम् एवम् आवृत्तिः, तदा काम्य-कर्मिणां किं वक्तव्यम् इति तान् निन्दन्न् आह षड्भिः । ये त्व् इह कर्म-स्वासक्त-मनसः सन्तोऽप्रतिषिद्धानि काम्यानि नित्यानि च कर्माणि कृत्स्नानि कुर्वन्ति, तेऽर्यम्णो दक्षिणेन पथा धूम-मार्गेण पितृ-लोकं व्रजन्तीति पञ्चमेनान्वयः । मध्ये तन्-निन्दा ॥१६॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: yadā brahmopāsakānām api bheda-darśanābhimānābhyām evam āvṛttiḥ, tadā kāmya-karmiṇāṃ kiṃ vaktavyam iti tān nindann āha ṣaḍbhiḥ | ye tv iha karma-svāsakta-manasaḥ santo’pratiṣiddhāni kāmyāni nityāni ca karmāṇi kṛtsnāni kurvanti, te’ryamṇo dakṣiṇena pathā dhūma-mārgeṇa pitṛ-lokaṃ vrajantīti pañcamenānvayaḥ | madhye tan-nindā ||16||
entries.literal_english: If even Brahman-worshippers return because of notions of difference and identity, what need be said of desire-motivated ritualists? Those whose minds are attached to actions perform all permitted desire-motivated and obligatory rites and travel by Aryaman’s southern path, the smoke-route, to Pitṛloka; the intervening verses censure them.

entries.sanskrit: हरति संसारं मेधा यस्य । कथनीया उरवो विक्रमा यस्य तस्य मधु-द्विषः कथायां विमुखाः सन्तो ये त्रैवर्गिकाः । ये चाच्युतस्य कथ-सुधां हित्वासतां गाथाः शृण्वन्ति ते नूनं दैवेन विहिता इत्य् अन्वयः ।।१८-१९॥
word_for_word: concerned with the three worldly aims
listen to tales of the unholy
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: harati saṃsāraṃ medhā yasya | kathanīyā uravo vikramā yasya tasya madhu-dviṣaḥ kathāyāṃ vimukhāḥ santo ye traivargikāḥ | ye cācyutasya katha-sudhāṃ hitvāsatāṃ gāthāḥ śṛṇvanti te nūnaṃ daivena vihitā ity anvayaḥ ||18-19||
entries.literal_english: Those concerned with the three worldly aims turn away from the narratives of Madhudviṣ, whose mighty deeds deserve telling and whose wisdom removes saṃsāra. Those who abandon the nectar of Acyuta’s stories and listen to tales of the unholy are surely disposed so by fate.

entries.sanskrit: पितृ-लोकात् पुनः प्रजाम् अनु स्व-पुत्रादिषु प्रजायन्ते । गर्भाधानाद् आरभ्य श्मशानान्ताः क्रियाः कृतवन्तः । यथोक्त-कारिण इत्य् अर्थः ॥२०॥
word_for_word: are born among their sons and descendants
rites ending at the cremation ground
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: pitṛ-lokāt punaḥ prajām anu sva-putrādiṣu prajāyante | garbhādhānād ārabhya śmaśānāntāḥ kriyāḥ kṛtavantaḥ | yathokta-kāriṇa ity arthaḥ ||20||
entries.literal_english: From Pitṛloka they are born again among their descendants such as their own sons. They had performed rites from conception through the cremation ground, meaning they acted according to prescription.

entries.sanskrit: कथं प्रजायन्ते ? तद् आह---ततस् ते पुनर् इमं लोकं प्रति पतन्ति । विभ्रंशित उदयो भोग-साधनं येषाम् ॥२१॥
word_for_word: ततस् ते पुनर् इमं लोकं प्रति पतन्ति
thereafter they fall back to this world
their prosperity and means of enjoyment have fallen away
for those whose means of enjoyment it was
entries.literal_english: How are they born? He answers: thereafter they fall back to this world; the means of enjoyment they had obtained have collapsed.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: kathaṃ prajāyante ? tad āha---tatas te punar imaṃ lokaṃ prati patanti | vibhraṃśita udayo bhoga-sādhanaṃ yeṣām ||21||

entries.sanskrit: परमेष्ठिनं परमेश्वरम् । सर्व-भावेनाति-प्रीत्या । तस्य गुणान् आश्रयते या भक्तिस् तया ॥२२॥
word_for_word: devotion that takes refuge in His qualities
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: parameṣṭhinaṃ parameśvaram | sarva-bhāvenāti-prītyā | tasya guṇān āśrayate yā bhaktis tayā ||22||
entries.literal_english: Parameṣṭhin here means the Supreme Lord. One worships Him with one’s whole being and intense love, through devotion that takes refuge in His qualities.

entries.sanskrit: भजने च ज्ञान-वैराग्ये स्वत एव भवत इत्य् आह---वासुदेव इति ॥२३॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: bhajane ca jñāna-vairāgye svata eva bhavata ity āha---vāsudeva iti ||23||
entries.literal_english: He says that in worship, knowledge and detachment arise of themselves.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवोपपादयति । यदास्य भक्तस्य चित्तं भगवद्-गुणानुरागेण तस्मिन्न् एव निश्चलं सद्-इन्द्रिय-वृत्तिभिर् वैषम्यम् अर्थेषु न विगृह्णाति ॥२४॥
word_for_word: does not grasp inequality among objects
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: tad evopapādayati | yadāsya bhaktasya cittaṃ bhagavad-guṇānurāgeṇa tasminn eva niścalaṃ sad-indriya-vṛttibhir vaiṣamyam artheṣu na vigṛhṇāti ||24||
entries.literal_english: He establishes this: when the devotee’s mind becomes steady in Bhagavān alone through attachment to His qualities, it no longer grasps inequality or differentiation among objects through the functions of the senses.

entries.sanskrit: तदैवात्मनात्मानं स्व-प्रकाशम् ईक्षते । कथं-भूतम् ? समं च तद्-दर्शनं च । तत् कुतः ? निःसङ्गम् । सङ्गाद् धि वैषम्यं भवति । निःसङ्गत्वे हेतुः---हेयोपादेय-रहितम् । तत् कुतः ? पदं व्यवसितम् आरूढम् । परमानन्दोऽहम् इति निश्चयं प्राप्तम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२५॥
word_for_word: at that very time, by the Self he sees the self-luminous Self
it is even, and its vision is even
the reason for nonattachment: it is free of what is to be rejected or taken up
how so? He has resolved upon and attained that state
परमानन्दोऽहम् इति निश्चयं प्राप्तम् इत्य् अर्थः
he has become certain “I am supreme bliss”; this is the meaning
entries.literal_english: At that very time, by the Self, he sees the Self, which is self-luminous. What is it like? It is even and its vision is even. Why? It is unattached, for attachment produces difference. Why is it unattached? It is free of what should be rejected and what should be taken up. How? He has resolved upon and attained that state, certain that “I am supreme bliss.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: tadaivātmanātmānaṃ sva-prakāśam īkṣate | kathaṃ-bhūtam ? samaṃ ca tad-darśanaṃ ca | tat kutaḥ ? niḥsaṅgam | saṅgād dhi vaiṣamyaṃ bhavati | niḥsaṅgatve hetuḥ---heyopādeya-rahitam | tat kutaḥ ? padaṃ vyavasitam ārūḍham | paramānando’ham iti niścayaṃ prāptam ity arthaḥ ||25||

entries.sanskrit: समेष्व् अर्थेष्व् इत्य् उक्तं तद् एव साम्यं दर्शयति । ज्ञान-मात्रम् एव पर-ब्रह्मादि-शब्दैः प्रसिद्धम् । दृश्य्-आदिभिर् दृश्य-द्रष्टृ-करण-रूपेण पृथक् प्रतीयते । ज्ञान-मात्रत्वेन समेष्व् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२६॥
word_for_word: known by terms such as Para-brahman
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: sameṣv artheṣv ity uktaṃ tad eva sāmyaṃ darśayati | jñāna-mātram eva para-brahmādi-śabdaiḥ prasiddham | dṛśy-ādibhir dṛśya-draṣṭṛ-karaṇa-rūpeṇa pṛthak pratīyate | jñāna-mātratvena sameṣv ity arthaḥ ||26||
entries.literal_english: He explains the equality just mentioned. Pure consciousness alone is known by terms such as Para-brahman. Through the seen, the seer, and the instruments it appears separately as these forms; but in truth all are equal as pure consciousness.

entries.sanskrit: ननु ज्ञान-मात्रम् आत्मनः स्वरूपत्वान् नित्य-प्राप्तम् एवेति किम् अनेक-साधन-साध्येन योगेन प्राप्यते तद् आह---एतावान् इति । युज्यते प्राप्यते । प्रपञ्च-सङ्ग-व्युद् आस एव योग-फलम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२७॥
word_for_word: pure consciousness is the Self’s nature
removal of attachment to the phenomenal world
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: nanu jñāna-mātram ātmanaḥ svarūpatvān nitya-prāptam eveti kim aneka-sādhana-sādhyena yogena prāpyate tad āha---etāvān iti | yujyate prāpyate | prapañca-saṅga-vyud āsa eva yoga-phalam ity arthaḥ ||27||
entries.literal_english: One might object that pure consciousness, being the Self’s nature, is eternally attained; why should yoga achieved by many disciplines attain it? The answer is that yoga’s fruit is simply the removal of attachment to the phenomenal world.

entries.sanskrit: ननु कथं प्रत्यक्षादि-प्रतीतः प्रपञ्चो व्युदसितुं शक्यते प्रतीतेर् भ्रान्तित्वात् ? इत्य् आह---ज्ञानम् इति । पराचीनैः पराङ्-मुखैः । शब्दादिर् धर्मो यस्य तेनार्थ-रूपेण ज्ञान-रूपं निर्गुणं ब्रह्मैवावभाति, न त्व् अर्थः पृथग् अस्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥२८॥
word_for_word: world appearing through perception and the like
qualified by sound and the like
Brahman as pure consciousness, without guṇas
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: nanu kathaṃ pratyakṣādi-pratītaḥ prapañco vyudasituṃ śakyate pratīter bhrāntitvāt ? ity āha---jñānam iti | parācīnaiḥ parāṅ-mukhaiḥ | śabdādir dharmo yasya tenārtha-rūpeṇa jñāna-rūpaṃ nirguṇaṃ brahmaivāvabhāti, na tv arthaḥ pṛthag astīty arthaḥ ||28||
entries.literal_english: How can the world established by perception and other means be removed? Because that appearance is erroneous. To outward-turned cognition, Brahman itself—pure consciousness and without guṇas—appears as an object qualified by sound and the like; no separate object exists apart from it.

entries.sanskrit: अर्थ-रूपत्वम् एवोदाहृत्य दर्शयति, यथेति । अहं-रूपोऽहङ्कारः । स च त्रि-वृत् त्रि-गुणात्मकः । पुनश् च भूत-रूपेण पञ्च-विधः, इन्द्रिय-रूपेणैकादश-विधश् च । स्वराड् जीव-रूपः । तस्य जीवस्य वपुर् अण्डं जगच् च । यतो येभो महद्-आदिभ्यः । तथावभाति ॥२९॥
word_for_word: ahaṅkāra in the form of I
from mahat and the other principles
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: artha-rūpatvam evodāhṛtya darśayati, yatheti | ahaṃ-rūpo’haṅkāraḥ | sa ca tri-vṛt tri-guṇātmakaḥ | punaś ca bhūta-rūpeṇa pañca-vidhaḥ, indriya-rūpeṇaikādaśa-vidhaś ca | svarāḍ jīva-rūpaḥ | tasya jīvasya vapur aṇḍaṃ jagac ca | yato yebho mahad-ādibhyaḥ | tathāvabhāti ||29||
entries.literal_english: He illustrates this appearance as objects. Ahaṅkāra has the form of “I” and is threefold through the three guṇas; it becomes fivefold as the elements and elevenfold as the senses. The self-ruling living being, its body, the cosmic egg, and the world all arise from mahat and the other principles and appear in this way.

entries.sanskrit: ननु तर्हि जनः किम् इत्य् एवं न प्रत्येति ? तत्राह---एतद् ब्रह्म ॥३०॥
word_for_word: जनः किम् इत्य् एवं न प्रत्येति
why do people not perceive it thus?
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: nanu tarhi janaḥ kim ity evaṃ na pratyeti ? tatrāha---etad brahma ||30||
entries.literal_english: One might ask why people do not perceive matters in this way. The answer begins, “This is Brahman.”

entries.sanskrit: उक्तम् एवार्थं सुख-प्रतिपत्त्य्-अर्थं सङ्क्षेपेणानुवदति---इतीति । हे गुर्वि पूज्ये ॥३१॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: uktam evārthaṃ sukha-pratipatty-arthaṃ saṅkṣepeṇānuvadati---itīti | he gurvi pūjye ||31||
entries.literal_english: For easy understanding he briefly restates the meaning already taught. “O gurvī” means O venerable lady.

entries.sanskrit: अनेन च ज्ञान-योगेन भगवान् एव प्राप्यो यथा भक्ति-योगेनेत्य् आह---नैर्गुण्यो ज्ञान-योगश् च मन्-निष्ठो भक्ति-लक्षणश् च यो योगस् तयोर् द्वयोर् अप्य् एक एवार्थः प्रयोजनम् । कोऽसौ । भगवच्-छब्दो लक्षणं ज्ञापको यस्य । तद् उक्तं गीतासु---ते प्राप्नुवन्ति माम् एव सर्व-भूत-हिते रताः\[गीता १२.४\] इति ॥३२॥
word_for_word: yoga characterized by devotion fixed on Me
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: anena ca jñāna-yogena bhagavān eva prāpyo yathā bhakti-yogenety āha---nairguṇyo jñāna-yogaś ca man-niṣṭho bhakti-lakṣaṇaś ca yo yogas tayor dvayor apy eka evārthaḥ prayojanam | ko’sau | bhagavac-chabdo lakṣaṇaṃ jñāpako yasya | tad uktaṃ gītāsu---te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ\[gītā 12.4\] iti ||32||
entries.literal_english: He says that Bhagavān is attained by this jñāna-yoga just as by bhakti-yoga. Guṇa-transcending jñāna-yoga and the yoga characterized by devotion fixed on Him have one and the same purpose: that whose indicator is the word Bhagavān. The Gītā likewise says that those devoted to the welfare of all beings attain Him alone.

entries.sanskrit: ननु ज्ञान-योगस्यात्म-लाभः फलं शस्त्रेणावगम्यते । भक्ति-योगस्य तु भजनीयेश्वर-प्राप्तिः । कुतस् तयोर् एकार्थत्वम् ? इत्य् आशङ्क्य दृष्टान्तेनोपपादयति---यथा बहूनां रूप-रसादीनां गुणानाम् आश्रयो गुड-क्षीरादिर् एक एवार्थो मार्ग-भेद-प्रवृत्तैर् इन्द्रियैर् नाना प्रतीयते । चक्षुषा शुक्ल इति, रसनेन मधुर इति, स्पर्शनेन शीत इत्य्-आदि, तथा भगवान् एक एव तत्-तद्-रूपेणावगम्यते ॥३३॥
word_for_word: realization of Self is jñāna-yoga’s fruit
attainment of the Lord is bhakti-yoga’s fruit
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: nanu jñāna-yogasyātma-lābhaḥ phalaṃ śastreṇāvagamyate | bhakti-yogasya tu bhajanīyeśvara-prāptiḥ | kutas tayor ekārthatvam ? ity āśaṅkya dṛṣṭāntenopapādayati---yathā bahūnāṃ rūpa-rasādīnāṃ guṇānām āśrayo guḍa-kṣīrādir eka evārtho mārga-bheda-pravṛttair indriyair nānā pratīyate | cakṣuṣā śukla iti, rasanena madhura iti, sparśanena śīta ity-ādi, tathā bhagavān eka eva tat-tad-rūpeṇāvagamyate ||33||
entries.literal_english: Though scripture gives realization of the Self as the fruit of jñāna-yoga and attainment of the worshipful Lord as the fruit of bhakti-yoga, the two have one object. Just as one substance such as sugar or milk, the support of many qualities, is apprehended differently by different senses—as white by the eye, sweet by the tongue, cool by touch—so the one Bhagavān is understood under those different aspects.

entries.sanskrit: शास्त्र-मार्गान् एव प्रपञ्चयति---क्रिययेति त्रिभिः । क्रियया पूर्त-रूपया । क्रतुभिर् यागैः । मर्शनं मीमांसा । आत्मेन्द्रिय-जयो निषिद्ध-वर्जनम् ॥३४॥
word_for_word: by works such as public-benefit rites
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: śāstra-mārgān eva prapañcayati---kriyayeti tribhiḥ | kriyayā pūrta-rūpayā | kratubhir yāgaiḥ | marśanaṃ mīmāṃsā | ātmendriya-jayo niṣiddha-varjanam ||34||
entries.literal_english: He expands the scriptural paths in three verses. Kriyā means works such as public-benefit rites; kratu means sacrifices; marśana means Mīmāṃsā inquiry; conquest of self and senses means abstaining from what is prohibited.

entries.sanskrit: उभय-चिह्नेन सकाम-निष्काम-लक्षणेन । तम् एवाह---य इति । स-काम-धर्म-प्राप्यं स्वर्गाद्य् अपि भगवत एव स-गुणं स्वरूपम् इति भावः ॥३५॥
word_for_word: by both marks, characterized by desire and desirelessness
even heaven and the rest attained through desire-driven duties
are the Lord’s own form endowed with qualities
entries.literal_english: “By both marks” means characterized by desire and desirelessness. He explains this with “he who.” Even heaven and other results of desire-driven duties are the Lord’s own form endowed with qualities; this is the meaning.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: ubhaya-cihnena sakāma-niṣkāma-lakṣaṇena | tam evāha---ya iti | sa-kāma-dharma-prāpyaṃ svargādy api bhagavata eva sa-guṇaṃ svarūpam iti bhāvaḥ ||35||

entries.sanskrit: एभिर् वर्त्मभिः । स्व-दृक् स्व-प्रकाशः ॥३६॥
entries.literal_english: “By these paths” means through these ways. “Self-seeing” means self-luminous.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: ebhir vartmabhiḥ | sva-dṛk sva-prakāśaḥ ||36||

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं ज्ञान-योगम् उपसंहृत्य तस्य च भक्ति-योगेन समानार्थत्वम् उक्त्वा भक्ति-योगाद्य् उपसंहरति---प्रावोचम् इति द्वाभ्याम् । चतुर्-विधं त्रि-गुण-निर्गुण-भेदेन । अन्तर्धावति उत्पत्ति-निधनादि करोति ॥३७॥
word_for_word: its having the same object as bhakti-yoga
through the three guṇas and nirguṇa
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: tad evaṃ jñāna-yogam upasaṃhṛtya tasya ca bhakti-yogena samānārthatvam uktvā bhakti-yogādy upasaṃharati---prāvocam iti dvābhyām | catur-vidhaṃ tri-guṇa-nirguṇa-bhedena | antardhāvati utpatti-nidhanādi karoti ||37||
entries.literal_english: Having concluded jñāna-yoga and stated that it has the same object as bhakti-yoga, he concludes the teachings beginning with bhakti-yoga. It is fourfold through the three guṇas and the nirguṇa form. “Moves within” means brings about origination, destruction, and the like.

entries.sanskrit: अङ्ग हे मातः ॥३८॥
entries.literal_english: “Aṅga” means “O Mother.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: aṅga he mātaḥ ||38||

entries.sanskrit: उपदेशेऽनधि-कारिणो दर्शयति, नैतद् इति द्वाभ्याम् । स्व-लाय परोद्वेजकाय । भिन्नाय दुराचाराय । धर्म-ध्वजाय दाम्भिकाय ॥३९-४०॥
word_for_word: hostile to self and disturbing to others
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: upadeśe’nadhi-kāriṇo darśayati, naitad iti dvābhyām | sva-lāya parodvejakāya | bhinnāya durācārāya | dharma-dhvajāya dāmbhikāya ||39-40||
entries.literal_english: In two verses he identifies those not qualified to receive this teaching: one hostile to oneself and disturbing to others, one morally corrupt, and a dharma-dhvaja, a hypocritical pretender to religion.

entries.sanskrit: अधिकारिण आह---श्रद्दधानायेति द्वाभ्याम् ॥४१॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
transliteration: adhikāriṇa āha---śraddadhānāyeti dvābhyām ||41||
entries.literal_english: In the two verses beginning “to one endowed with faith,” he states who is qualified to receive the teaching.

entries.sanskrit: एतच्-छ्रवण-कीर्तन-परस्यापि मत्-पद-प्राप्तिर् एव फलम् इत्य् आह---य इति । अप्य्-अर्थे च-कारः । सोऽपि मत्-पदवीम् एति । हि निश्चितम् ॥४३॥
word_for_word: even for one devoted to hearing and chanting this
attaining my feet alone is the result
the particle “ca” is used in the sense of “also”
that person too reaches my abode
entries.literal_english: He says that even for one devoted to hearing and chanting this, attaining my feet alone is the result. The particle “ca” has the sense of “also”: that person too reaches my abode. This is certain.

transliteration: etac-chravaṇa-kīrtana-parasyāpi mat-pada-prāptir eva phalam ity āha---ya iti | apy-arthe ca-kāraḥ | so’pi mat-padavīm eti | hi niścitam ||43||
